_meta.note: Hand-maintained topic tags for `just topic <term>`. Everything else that command reports is DERIVED (verb section, element name, grep), so it needs no maintenance and cannot go stale. This file exists only for the items a topic cannot reach by name: a skin element called `rhythmzone` is part of the waveform surface and says so nowhere. Tags are a navigation aid, never evidence — a tag makes an item findable, it claims nothing about what the item does.
_meta.why_not_a_field_on_each_record: Topics are cross-cutting, so a `topics: []` field per verb record would scatter one topic's membership across a thousand records and make it unreviewable. It would also put a navigation aid into the store that is authoritative for per-verb EVIDENCE. One map, reviewed as a whole, is the maintainable shape.
_meta.checked_by: tools/topic.py check — every name here must exist in the verb store, the XML inventory, or docs/, and every alias must point at a defined topic

waveform.why: the elements that draw the waveform surface do not carry the word — `rhythmzone`, `scratchwave`, `zoomed` and `songpos` are all invisible to a name search for `waveform`

browser.why: the browser is assembled from a dozen elements, most of which are named after the part rather than the browser

sampler.why: the sampler's own XML format and its skin elements use `sample`/`slot`, not `sampler`

pads.why: a pad page's structural elements are named for their role, not for pads

mouse.why: hit-area and clipping shaping is spread across six differently named elements, and nothing groups them

states.why: an element's visual states are child elements with bare names — `on`, `over`, `down` — that a topic search will never reach

menu.why: menus are built from `item` and `submenu`, neither of which contains the word

fonts.why: the browser's per-zone font overrides are named for the zone

colorfx.why: reachable by name, but the alias table folds `color fx` and the British spellings into it

hotcue.why: the skin elements are `cue`/`cues`, and the verb is spelled both ways

cue.why: same surface as hotcue, reachable under either word

loop.why: the skin element is the plural `loops`, which a singular search misses

mapper.why: the mapper format's elements are `map`/`mapper`/`info`, and controller work reaches for the word `controller`

stems.why: stem controls live under Equalizer & Stems and several are named for the part

video.why: the video skin family has its own element vocabulary that a name search does not join up
